gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at maker prices on 2026-11-13, the WEN GN875i (120/240V L14-30R, 7,000 rated W, $899.99 at wenproducts.com) costs $0.13 per running watt. That beats ChatGPT's 'best value' Westinghouse ecoGen10000, which costs $0.17/W because Westinghouse's own store asks $1,299, not the $1,149 ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: I compared the cited lightsonlabs.com page and the top results homewelder.com and rightgenerator.com; consumerreports.org was paywalled and showed no models. Lights On Labs lists only the Honda EU7000iS as a 240V inverter ($4,899). Homewelder prices the Champion 201175 ($1,594.07) and DuroMax XP11000iH ($2,499) but leaves the iGen12000DFc unpriced. Rightgenerator gives the iGen8200TFc as $1,399, but Westinghouse now asks $1,599. None of the three pages computes price per running watt, and none names the WEN GN875i, WEN TF1300iX or Westinghouse iGen12000DFc/TFc with maker prices.
decides: This challenges ChatGPT's 'best value' pick. On running watts per dollar at maker prices, the WEN GN875i ($0.129/W) and WEN DF680iX ($0.158/W) both beat the ecoGen10000 ($0.171/W). The Westinghouse store's product feed also marked the ecoGen10000, iGen12000DFc, iGen12000TFc and iGen8200TFc as unavailable today, though I could not confirm this on the rendered page. ChatGPT's dual-fuel, tri-fuel and quiet picks still hold on price: Champion 201417 $1,999.99, WEN TF1050iX $1,649 and Honda EU7000iS $4,899 (the top of ChatGPT's $4,500–$4,900 range).
